def Target : Prop :=
  ∀ (X Y : Type) (P : S2 X Y) (T : ℕ),
    ∃ N : S1 X Y, N.D9 ∧ N.d13 = T ∧
      ∀ xs : List X, xs.length ≤ T → N.d4 xs = P.d4 xs
a_raw: {"translation": "`Target` defines a proposition (it names a `Prop` without asserting or proving it) stating that: for all types `X` and `Y`, for every system `P : S2 X Y`—consisting of two state types `B1` and `B2`, initial states `b3 : B1` and `b4 : B2`, transition functions `b6 : B1 → B2 → X → B1` and `b5 : B1 → B2 → X → B2`, and an output function `a6 : B2 → Y`—and for every natural number `T : ℕ`, there exists a system `N : S1 X Y` (which may depend on `X`, `Y`, `P`, and `T`) consisting of a finite index type `N.A1` (with finiteness witness `N.a2`), a family of local state types `N.A3 : N.A1 → Type`, an initial global state `N.a4 : (n : N.A1) → N.A3 n`, local update functions `N.a5 : (n : N.A1) → ((m : N.A1) → N.A3 m) → X → N.A3 n`, and an output function `N.a6 : ((m : N.A1) → N.A3 m) → Y`, such that all three of the following hold: (1) Acyclicity of functional state-update dependence (`N.D9`): defining a directed relation `N.D8 m n` to hold iff there exist two global states `σ, σ' : (k : N.A1) → N.A3 k` and an input `x : X` such that `σ k = σ' k` for all `k ≠ m` and `N.a5 n σ x ≠ N.a5 n σ' x`, there is no `n : N.A1` with a nonempty directed chain `n = c_0, c_1, ..., c_k = n` (`k ≥ 1`) satisfying `N.D8 c_i c_{i+1}` at every step (ruling out both self-loops `N.D8 n n` and longer cycles). (2) Exact cardinality (`N.d13 = T`): the finite type `N.A1` has cardinality exactly `T` (`Fintype.card N.A1 = T`). (3) Input-output agreement up to length `T`: for every finite list `xs : List X` with `xs.length ≤ T`, `N.d4 xs = P.d4 xs`, where `N.d4 xs` starts from `N.a4`, updates the global state left-to-right for each `x` in `xs` via `σ ↦ (fun n => N.a5 n σ x)`, and applies `N.a6` to the resulting global state, while `P.d4 xs` starts from `(P.b3, P.b4)`, updates the pair left-to-right for each `x` in `xs` via `(s1, s2) ↦ (P.b6 s1 s2 x, P.b5 s1 s2 x)`, and applies `P.a6` to the second (`B2`) component of the resulting pair. What is and is not required: `X`, `Y`, `P.B1`, `P.B2`, and the local state types `N.A3 n` are completely unconstrained types (none need be finite, nonempty, or bounded in size); `T` may be any natural number, including `0` (in which case `N.A1` must be empty); the component count `Fintype.card N.A1` must equal `T` exactly rather than merely be at most `T`; `N` is chosen after `T` (and after `X`, `Y`, `P`); agreement between `N.d4` and `P.d4` is required only for sequences of length at most `T` (nothing is required for lengths greater than `T`); no internal state correspondence between `N` and `P` is required; and the acyclicity condition `N.D9` constrains only `N.a5`, placing no restriction on `N.a6`."}
translation: `Target` defines a proposition (it names a `Prop` without asserting or proving it) stating that: for all types `X` and `Y`, for every system `P : S2 X Y`—consisting of two state types `B1` and `B2`, initial states `b3 : B1` and `b4 : B2`, transition functions `b6 : B1 → B2 → X → B1` and `b5 : B1 → B2 → X → B2`, and an output function `a6 : B2 → Y`—and for every natural number `T : ℕ`, there exists a system `N : S1 X Y` (which may depend on `X`, `Y`, `P`, and `T`) consisting of a finite index type `N.A1` (with finiteness witness `N.a2`), a family of local state types `N.A3 : N.A1 → Type`, an initial global state `N.a4 : (n : N.A1) → N.A3 n`, local update functions `N.a5 : (n : N.A1) → ((m : N.A1) → N.A3 m) → X → N.A3 n`, and an output function `N.a6 : ((m : N.A1) → N.A3 m) → Y`, such that all three of the following hold: (1) Acyclicity of functional state-update dependence (`N.D9`): defining a directed relation `N.D8 m n` to hold iff there exist two global states `σ, σ' : (k : N.A1) → N.A3 k` and an input `x : X` such that `σ k = σ' k` for all `k ≠ m` and `N.a5 n σ x ≠ N.a5 n σ' x`, there is no `n : N.A1` with a nonempty directed chain `n = c_0, c_1, ..., c_k = n` (`k ≥ 1`) satisfying `N.D8 c_i c_{i+1}` at every step (ruling out both self-loops `N.D8 n n` and longer cycles). (2) Exact cardinality (`N.d13 = T`): the finite type `N.A1` has cardinality exactly `T` (`Fintype.card N.A1 = T`). (3) Input-output agreement up to length `T`: for every finite list `xs : List X` with `xs.length ≤ T`, `N.d4 xs = P.d4 xs`, where `N.d4 xs` starts from `N.a4`, updates the global state left-to-right for each `x` in `xs` via `σ ↦ (fun n => N.a5 n σ x)`, and applies `N.a6` to the resulting global state, while `P.d4 xs` starts from `(P.b3, P.b4)`, updates the pair left-to-right for each `x` in `xs` via `(s1, s2) ↦ (P.b6 s1 s2 x, P.b5 s1 s2 x)`, and applies `P.a6` to the second (`B2`) component of the resulting pair. What is and is not required: `X`, `Y`, `P.B1`, `P.B2`, and the local state types `N.A3 n` are completely unconstrained types (none need be finite, nonempty, or bounded in size); `T` may be any natural number, including `0` (in which case `N.A1` must be empty); the component count `Fintype.card N.A1` must equal `T` exactly rather than merely be at most `T`; `N` is chosen after `T` (and after `X`, `Y`, `P`); agreement between `N.d4` and `P.d4` is required only for sequences of length at most `T` (nothing is required for lengths greater than `T`); no internal state correspondence between `N` and `P` is required; and the acyclicity condition `N.D9` constrains only `N.a5`, placing no restriction on `N.a6`.

divergences.description: In `S1`, every unit receives the external input `x` directly at every time step, the output function `a6` is an arbitrary readout over all units' states (unconstrained by `D9`), and unit state spaces `A3 n` are arbitrary (possibly infinite) types; conversely, `D9` forbids self-loops so individual units cannot read their own previous states, making the informal description "arbitrary state machines" slightly loose.

When summarizing the passages, the description characterizes plasticity in the paper's sense as parameters changing "between time steps" (a discrete-time idealization, whereas [P-O3] speaks of parameters changing "over time" and equivalence breaking "for all t > t0") and trims the qualifiers "rapid" ([P-O1], "rapid plasticity negates the functional equivalence") and "nontrivial" ([P-O3], "any nontrivial plasticity").

judgement.summary: The Lean statement accurately formalizes the author's description with matching quantifiers, two-component dynamics, exact unit count, acyclicity, and finite-horizon output agreement, and the description accurately and candidly represents what the passages claim and concede. Only minor presentational and idealization caveats apply regarding `S1`'s unrestricted input broadcast/readout and informal phrasing.
